market: City of Columbus, OH (issuing jurisdiction only)
note: PREDECLARED before any evaluation result, backtest, or metric was computed or seen. Provisional and un-calibrated. Thresholds here MUST NOT be changed after seeing results (roadmap P2.2); a post-hoc edit changes this file's hash and the manifest thresholds_id, so tuning is detectable. If the evidence is inconclusive, the decision is HOLD, not a validation claim. This file is intended to be hashed and pinned exactly like fixtures/thresholds.devvelocity-v0.json; values that also appear there (firing_threshold, baseline_move, signal_frequency, lead_time_comparator) MUST match that file and never drift.

qualified_historical_corpus_P0_8.rationale: A real evaluation additionally requires a qualified, rights-cleared historical Columbus corpus (roadmap P0.8) with reproducible dates/units/stages/dedupe/gaps and honest first_observed_at/recorded_at. That corpus is NOT yet available, so this protocol can be predeclared but NOT yet executed as a validation.

score_is_validated.rationale: The development-velocity-v0 0-100 score stays UNVALIDATED. It has no empirical calibration, no mapping to investment outcome, and is not comparable across markets. This protocol does not change that; passing it is a P2.2/P2.3 prerequisite, not an assertion.

value.name: sustained_elevated_activity
value.definition: For a signal that FIRED at cutoff T (known_then only), the outcome is POSITIVE iff the observed per-window permit count, for the same pinned source and the same pinned attribute (permit.filed_at XOR permit.issued_at), is >= the trailing baseline mean computed as-of T (baseline_mean_observed_records at T) in EACH of the next H consecutive 30-day windows that fall strictly after T's current window. Otherwise the outcome is NEGATIVE (activity reverted / was not sustained).
value.comparison_level: per_pinned_source (counts are never summed across sources)
value.outcome_window: strictly_after_T: windows w_k = [T + k*30d, T + (k+1)*30d) for k in 1..H, each ending at or before the evaluation cutoff
value.cutoff_safety: The outcome is read ONLY through activity_baseline()/observations_as_of at as_of = T_eval, so it uses only observations eligible (first_observed_at <= T_eval, recorded_at <= T_eval, received_at <= T_eval) and the latest interpretation known as-of T_eval. It therefore uses only information that became available strictly after T and never leaks a future correction dated after T_eval.
value.evaluable_requirement: A fired signal is EVALUABLE only if all H post-T windows end at or before the end of the qualified corpus; signals whose outcome window is not fully observed are reported as not_yet_evaluable and excluded from rates.

outcome_definition.rationale: Honest, measurable, cutoff-safe outcome: 'did the elevated activity persist, or did it immediately revert?' H is a fixed integer (3 months) chosen before any result. No forward-looking or price/deal outcome is claimed in v0; this measures persistence of the measured quantity only.

horizon_days.rationale: H = 3 monthly (30-day) windows = 90 days. Fixed integer set before tuning; un-tunable post-hoc.

simple_baseline_comparator.rationale: The lead-time/naive comparator is the existing descriptive trailing comparator app/services/activity_baseline.py (its baseline_periods trailing windows), run as-of the same cutoffs through the same cutoff-safe driver (driver.baseline_run). It 'crosses' when a source's current window >= baseline_move * baseline mean. baseline_move = 2.0 matches fixtures/thresholds.devvelocity-v0.json and must not drift.

lead_time_comparator.rationale: Lead time is the signed days between the first known_then cutoff at which development-velocity-v0 fires and the first cutoff at which the trailing comparator crosses baseline_move. Predeclared acceptance floor: the signal must not LAG the naive comparator (median lead >= 0 days). This is a comparison only; it is not an assertion the lead is real or significant (needs outcomes + sample sizes).

false_positive_tolerance.false_positive_definition: A known_then fired, evaluable signal whose sustained_elevated_activity outcome is NEGATIVE (activity reverted below the T baseline mean within H).
false_positive_tolerance.rationale: Provisional maximum acceptable false-positive rate: at most one third of evaluable fired signals may revert within H. Above this, the signal is not acceptable at this threshold. Un-calibrated; predeclared before any result; must not be tuned afterward. Exceeding it, or an inconclusive sample, means HOLD.

signal_frequency.rationale: Fraction of known-then eligible cutoffs where the signal fires. A signal that fires on more than half of eligible cutoffs is too trigger-happy to be informative. Sanity bound, not a validation target. Matches fixtures/thresholds.devvelocity-v0.json.

min_sample_size.rationale: Below EITHER floor the evaluation MUST return 'inconclusive_insufficient_sample' and make NO validation claim (HOLD). Floors are conservative-but-small because Columbus is a single market with <2 complete years of qualified commercial history: a 6-window baseline warm-up (~6 months) plus a 3-window outcome tail (~3 months) consumes most of the usable span, and overlapping monthly windows are autocorrelated so nominal counts overstate independent evidence. min_evaluable_periods=12 requires at least a year of evaluable known_then cutoffs; min_fired_signals=5 prevents a validation claim from a handful of fires. These are necessary, not sufficient: meeting them still only permits a measured result, never an automatic pass.

value.reserved_for: out_of_sample_reporting; excluded from any future threshold-setting or revision

holdout_periods.rationale: Single-market temporal holdout: the most recent contiguous 6 monthly windows of the qualified Columbus corpus are reserved. Because every threshold here is predeclared (not fit to data), the holdout is the out-of-sample window on which metrics are reported and against which any future threshold revision is forbidden. Reserved before any result was seen.

holdout_markets.rationale: Columbus is the only qualified market, so a market (geography) holdout is impossible in v0. Market holdouts become required future work once >=2 markets qualify under roadmap P0.8 (the other four markets). Until then, only the temporal holdout above applies and no cross-market generalization is claimed.

firing_threshold.rationale: development-velocity-v0 fires when the 0-100 score >= 70 (~2 baseline SD above the trailing mean, since score = 50 + 10*clamp(z, +/-5)). PROVISIONAL, UNVALIDATED research cutoff, declared before any replay result; mirrors and must match fixtures/thresholds.devvelocity-v0.json. Frozen for a run via the manifest thresholds_id and copied into series.params (part of run_fingerprint). MUST NOT be tuned after seeing results.

decision_rule.rationale: The evaluation yields a measured result only; it renders no automatic keep/revise/kill (that is the independent P2.3 go/no-go). If min_sample_size floors are not met, OR the false-positive rate exceeds false_positive_tolerance, OR the median lead is below min_median_lead_days, OR the result is otherwise inconclusive, the decision is HOLD (roadmap P2.3: inconclusive evidence means hold, not predictive marketing). Thresholds cannot be chosen after seeing results.
